clue.text: Threesome finally toast with port

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word toast, its closing letter

parts.note: last letter of toast
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Someone raises a last glass of port to drink a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three people or things, exactly a threesome.

clue.text: Understood Sun altered useless articles by newsman

indicators.note: altered says the three letters of Sun are changed into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
tat is cheap, worthless goods or junk
ED, short for editor, a crossword newsman

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper's tinkering produces junk stories from its editor, the implication being left unsaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges SUN into UNS; TAT is British slang for tacky junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstated is implied or tacitly understood rather than said outright.

clue.text: Measuring device worker tracks sometime in autumn?

indicators.note: tracks means follows, so the worker comes after the month

parts.note: Oct., October, a month in the northern autumn
the worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A surveying instrument is used by a labourer on railway tracks one autumn day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracks' looks like railway lines but is a verb meaning follows, so the insect comes after the month.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is a navigational instrument for measuring angles, a forerunner of the sextant.

clue.text: Very cold, heron-like bird emitting note

indicators.note: emitting means giving out, so the note is let go from the bird's name

parts.note: the bittern is a wading bird of the heron family
N for note, a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A shivering heron-like bird gives out its call in freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind or winter is piercingly, intensely cold.

clue.text: Part of car seat salesperson lifted

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside, the part you sit on

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised, so the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A car seat is stolen by a salesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the bum is the bottom, so 'seat' means BUM, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper is the protective bar at the front or back of a car.

clue.text: Expend great effort and time on painting

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: An artist labours for ages on a single picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to work extremely hard and long, to labour.

clue.text: Uniform on lad good for religious service

parts.note: uniform means regular, consistent: even
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A uniform worn by a boy is suitable for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' reads as clothing but is an adjective meaning EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

clue.text: Top wine, one thousand pounds, rowing team picked up

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the next word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a crew is the team in a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A rowing team buys a thousand-pound bottle of fine wine to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW sounds like the French CRU, a vineyard's classification.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand cru is a French classification for the finest vineyards, so the wine is top quality.

clue.text: Chaps coming across to assist racehorse without a win

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so the men go round the other piece

parts.note: chaps are men
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: Some men come over to help a horse that never wins.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing a maiden is a horse that has not yet won a race.

clue.text: British backing also affected military training centre

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for also runs backwards

parts.note: too means also
camp means exaggerated, theatrically affected

explanation.surface: British support for some affected military base.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is where military recruits receive their basic training.

clue.text: Leave out distinguished medal, Italian

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, a British honour for distinguished service
It. is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian is left out when a distinguished medal is awarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an exclusive British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to exclude or leave something out.

clue.text: Came up with Al incorrectly — it's my fault

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of these words are set wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after coming up with a wrong answer for Al.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'through my fault', an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Jack prepared mainly orange seasoning

parts.note: jack and tar both mean a sailor

indicators.note: prepared says the letters are worked into a fresh order, as food is made ready
mainly means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: the fruit word, missing its tail

explanation.surface: A sailor cooks a dish that is mostly orange-flavoured seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' leaves ORANG, which 'prepared' rearranges into RAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic herb used to flavour food.

clue.text: Sack a former partner wanting a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means going upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Someone fires a former partner who asked for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a rise' reads as a salary request, but in a down clue it turns EX upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the axe is to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Character on keyboard deviously tries to put in request

indicators.note: put in says the rearranged letters are placed inside the request

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: deviously means by a crooked route, so the letters of tries are twisted round

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly tries to slip a keyboard symbol into a formal request.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go after the first two letters of the request word, not in the exact middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The asterisk is the star-shaped symbol typed above the 8 key.

clue.text: English painter captures revelry occasionally

parts.note: to land a fish or a contract is to capture it

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of revelry counts

parts.note: its alternate letters

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a scene of merrymaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth and sixth letters of revelry gives EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian artist famous for animals and the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: Assist Cockney when round US city

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H at the start of words, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: to help is to assist
as means when, as in 'as I left'
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A Londoner helps out when going round an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Rank administered by police force

parts.note: to run an organisation is to administer it
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Someone's rank is assigned by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a police grade but is an adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank food smells offensively stale, just like rancid butter.

clue.text: Upon retirement, received a one-piece garment

indicators.note: retirement is drawing back, so the word for received is read backwards

parts.note: got means received

explanation.surface: On retiring, someone is presented with a single-piece robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-piece' may look like a description, but 'one' is the A here.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose draped outer robe of a Roman citizen.

clue.text: Levy on one vehicle

parts.note: a levy is a tax
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A charge is imposed on a single vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car hired with its driver for a journey.

clue.text: Method of cooking father and friend reinvented

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: reinvented means made over afresh, so the letters of friend are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Dad and a pal come up with a new recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is adjectival, a description of the cooking method rather than a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan-fried describes food cooked in a shallow frying pan with a little fat.

clue.text: Famous school event's outside, happening

indicators.note: outside means only the outer letters of the word event are kept

parts.note: the word event, its first and last letters
on means taking place, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: An outdoor event takes place at a well-known school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a possessive: the outside of event is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is England's best-known public school, near Windsor.

clue.text: Returning in Cadillac: a placid South American creature

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A calm animal heads back home in a Cadillac.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is what signals that the letters are concealed within 'Cadillac: a placid'.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated camelid of the Andes, prized for its wool.

clue.text: Slovenly cricket fielder, Henry, covered in some turf

parts.note: slip is a close catching position beside the wicketkeeper

indicators.note: covered in says the letter is wrapped inside the piece of turf

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A sloppy cricket fielder named Henry is buried under turf.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket fielding position next to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is careless and untidy, done without proper attention.

clue.text: Business admits a transgression — gambling's prevalent here

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the business takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: A firm confesses wrongdoing in a culture where gambling is common.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building devoted to gaming tables and betting.
